question_text: Over the last two weeks, how often have you had little interest or pleasure in doing things you usually enjoy?
Over the last two weeks, how often have you felt down, depressed, discouraged, or hopeless?
How often have you felt bad about yourself — or felt that you are a failure, or have let yourself or your family down?
How often have you felt tired, sluggish, or depleted of physical and mental energy?
Have you noticed moving or speaking so slowly that other people could have noticed, or conversely being unusually restless?
When you wake up in the morning, do you experience a persistent emotional heaviness before the day begins?
How would you describe the general emotional climate of your thoughts over the past two weeks?
Have you found yourself crying or feeling unusually tearful without an obvious trigger?
How often do you feel completely emotionally numb or disconnected from the people around you?
When something positive happens in your life, can you genuinely feel joy, or does it pass through without resonance?
Do you find yourself feeling guilty about things that are outside of your control?
Have you noticed feelings of irritability, short temper, or frustration over minor inconveniences?
How frequently do you experience a sense of emptiness or like you are just going through the motions?
What is one thought or feeling that has been lingering in your mind most intensely today?
Do you feel that you have been carrying emotional burdens without a safe outlet to unpack them?
Over the past month, have you felt that your mood swings rapidly between sadness, anger, and numbness?
How often do you feel that life has become a relentless struggle rather than an experience to participate in?
If your current mood had a weather forecast, how would you describe it right now?
Over the last two weeks, how often have you felt nervous, anxious, or on edge?
How often have you not been able to stop or control worrying?
How often have you worried too much about different things in your life?
How often have you had trouble relaxing even when you had free time?
How often have you been so restless that it is hard to sit still?
How often have you become easily annoyed, irritable, or snappy?
How often have you felt afraid, as if something awful or catastrophic might happen?
Have you experienced sudden episodes of intense terror, heart racing, shortness of breath, or shaking (panic episodes)?
Do physical sensations like chest tightness, dizziness, or stomach butterflies frequently accompany your worry?
Do you find yourself actively avoiding conversations, places, or responsibilities because they trigger anxiety?
When you have to speak in social settings or meeting people, how intensely do you fear being judged or embarrassed?
Do repetitive intrusive thoughts enter your mind that feel hard to dismiss or dismissive of logic?
What situation or upcoming event triggers the strongest sense of unease or dread for you right now?
Do you catch yourself holding your breath or breathing shallowly throughout the workday?
How often do you replay past conversations in your head, criticizing what you said or didn't say?
Does your anxiety feel like an alarm bell constantly ringing in your nervous system?
In the last month, how often have you felt that you were unable to control the important things in your life?
How often have you felt difficulties were piling up so high that you could not overcome them?
Are demands from your work, family, or personal responsibilities feeling unsustainable right now?
What is the single heaviest source of pressure on your shoulders at this point in your life?
When stress peaks, what is the first coping behavior you instinctively turn to?
Have you noticed relying on alcohol, nicotine, caffeine, or substances more frequently to manage your stress?
Do you feel that you have adequate time during the week for decompression and mental silence?
How often do you feel tense in your jaw, neck, shoulders, or back due to persistent strain?
Do you feel pressure to always appear strong, cheerful, or productive even when suffering inside?
Have you experienced emotional outbursts of crying, yelling, or withdrawing when small things go wrong?
Do financial or health uncertainties currently pose a major challenge to your peace of mind?
When you face a difficult problem, do you usually break it into steps, or do you feel paralyzed?
Have you taken any personal days or deliberate breaks for your mental wellbeing in the past three months?
On a scale of 0 to 3, how overwhelmed has your nervous system felt across the past week?
Over the last two weeks, how often have you had trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or sleeping too much?
On average, how many hours of actual restful sleep do you achieve each night?
When your head hits the pillow, does your mind start racing with worries, to-do lists, or existential dilemmas?
Do you frequently wake up in the middle of the night (e.g. 2:00 AM - 4:00 AM) and find it difficult to fall back asleep?
Do you wake up early in the morning hours feeling an immediate surge of dread or sorrow?
Even after what should be a full night of sleep, do you still wake up feeling physically and mentally unrefreshed?
Have you been experiencing intense, distressing nightmares or fragmented dream states recently?
Do you find yourself sleeping excessively (more than 10-11 hours) as an unconscious way to escape the waking day?
Do you use sleeping pills, over-the-counter sedatives, or nighttime alcohol to initiate sleep?
How consistent is your sleep-wake schedule between workdays and weekends?
Does daytime drowsiness or brain fog impair your concentration or ability to drive/work safely?
Do you engage with bright phone or computer screens directly before turning off the lights to sleep?
What single change in your sleep routine would make the biggest difference in your daily wellbeing?
Overall, how satisfied are you with the depth and quality of your rest over the past month?
Over the last two weeks, how often have you had poor appetite, or found yourself overeating comfort foods?
Over the last two weeks, how often have you had trouble concentrating on things, such as reading the news, studying, or watching television?
How difficult have your emotional or physical symptoms made it to do your work, take care of things at home, or get along with other people?
Have you struggled to initiate basic self-care routines like showering, brushing teeth, eating balanced meals, or tidying up?
Do you find yourself procrastinating on important responsibilities due to mental fatigue or cognitive overwhelm?
Have you been canceling plans, avoiding phone calls, or declining invitations to see friends or family?
Have you missed days from work, university, or school in the past month due to mental or emotional distress?
When at work or studying, do you feel like you are working at your normal capacity, or is there a noticeable drop?
Do you feel motivated by personal goals, curiosity, or future milestones right now?
Have you experienced frequent unexplainable physical complaints like headaches, stomach aches, or muscle soreness?
How would you rate your ability to make everyday decisions without getting stuck in second-guessing?
Are you able to maintain healthy boundaries and say 'no' when your schedule or energy is maxed out?
What is one activity that usually leaves you feeling accomplished or restored when you finish it?
Do you feel that your daily life provides you with a sense of rhythm and purpose, or does it feel chaotic?
Over the last two weeks, have you had thoughts that you would be better off dead, or thoughts of hurting yourself in some way?
Have you had active thoughts of ending your life or wishing that you would not wake up in the morning?
Have you developed any specific plan, thought about a method, or considered a timeline for harming yourself?
Do you currently have access to lethal means, medications, or instruments that you have considered using?
Have you engaged in any deliberate self-injury (such as cutting, burning, or hitting yourself) in the past month to cope with pain?
Have you ever attempted suicide in the past or required hospitalization for self-harm?
Do you currently feel safe in your home environment, or are you experiencing physical, emotional, or domestic abuse?
Have you had thoughts or urges to physically harm another person or damage property?
Do you ever experience voices, visions, or beliefs that other people cannot hear or understand?
Do you feel that you can keep yourself safe right now until you can speak with a healthcare professional or trusted contact?
Is there someone in your immediate life who you could call or stay with right now if distress became unbearable?
What is one reason or commitment that keeps you holding on even when the emotional pain feels overwhelming?
Do you have at least one person in your life (friend, family member, mentor) who listens without judgment?
Have you ever spoken with a psychologist, counselor, or psychiatrist in the past?
How open do you feel to speaking with a licensed mental health professional (online or in-person) if a referral is suggested?
What quality do you look for most in a psychologist or therapist (e.g. warmth, practical tools, language, gender)?
Which consultation format would you feel most comfortable with right now: confidential video call or an in-clinic visit?
What is a personal strength, value, or past obstacle that reminds you of your resilience?
Do you engage in any grounding practices like prayer, meditation, walking in nature, or creative arts?
Do you have pets, hobbies, or community projects that bring warmth and connection to your routine?
When you think about the next six months, is there an aspiration or milestone that you still look forward to experiencing?
Would you find it helpful to receive guided 4-7-8 breathing exercises and evidence-based self-compassion tools?
If you had a close friend feeling the way you feel today, what compassionate words would you say to them?
How comfortable do you feel taking this conversation as a brave, compassionate first step toward honoring your wellbeing?
